plans.note: No liability heading surfaced in the outline, but hosting agreements of this type usually bury a cap/consequential-damages waiver in the general body under sec-p0001; check the misc/administrative block near sec-5.4 before concluding it is missing. HDI is the vendor, so any cap must be mutual and carve out IP, confidentiality and misconduct.

Scan the body under sec-p0001 for an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP claims arising from the developed/hosted site and HDI's own misconduct; confirm any reciprocal Deerskin indemnity is limited to content we supply.

Given the affiliate-style HDI/Deerskin relationship and the defined term 'Deerskin Products', check the body for any restriction on the lines of business Deerskin may operate or the channels through which it may sell; such a restraint on us would be a deviation.

A site development and hosting arrangement commonly makes HDI the sole provider of site development/hosting; look in the scope-of-services text around sec-1.4 for language barring us from engaging other developers or hosts.
Nothing in the outline suggests pricing parity or best-terms language; confirm by scanning the fee provisions in the body, but an MFN running against us is unlikely here.

Section 5.4 deals with each party appointing a representative/personnel interface, so any employee non-solicit is most likely adjacent to it; test for duration, scope and a general-advertising carve-out if found.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms a termination construct exists in the body under sec-p0001; verify we may exit on notice without penalty and that HDI cannot terminate hosting mid-term at will.
The 'Termination Date' definition points to a fixed term rather than an evergreen renewal; check the term provisions in the body, but auto-renewal and a notice window appear not to be used.
Governing law will sit in the boilerplate immediately before the signature block at sec-p0072; New York or Delaware would be acceptable, and confirm courts rather than arbitration.
Look in the closing boilerplate near sec-p0072 for assignment/successors language; we need affiliate and successor assignment rights and no HDI termination right on our change of control.

Section 1.4 governs the access HDI provides and is the natural home for ownership of the site, deliverables and Deerskin data; confirm we own the developed site content and customer/order data and that nothing assigns our IP to HDI.
The access grant in sec-1.4 is the likely licence clause; check it extends to our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at HDI's discretion.
No audit or records heading appears; if a records provision exists it is more likely an audit of HDI's fees in our favour, which we would not flag.
No fee or damages heading surfaced; scan the payment terms for any stipulated damages or penalty payable by Deerskin, but none is indicated.

Check the services/performance text around sec-1.4 and the body for an HDI warranty on development work and hosting availability, plus a repair/re-perform remedy; also watch for a broad disclaimer of all warranties.
No insurance heading in the outline; HDI hosts our site and data, so if the body is silent this should be raised as missing.
Check the fee provisions for any minimum spend, guaranteed volume of Deerskin Products or take-or-pay hosting charge; nothing in the outline signals one.
Tie to the 'Termination Date' definition: look for post-termination return of site content, customer data and files, and migration assistance from HDI; sec-1.4 access rights may carry over.
